history.summary: NOTE: the CSV name 'Shri Swaminarayan Temple, Surat' is ambiguous - Surat has multiple Swaminarayan temples (BAPS and other diocese shrines). This record documents the prominent BAPS mandir at Adajan; if the CSV intends a different shrine, it needs re-mapping. The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir at Pramukh Swami Maharaj Marg, Swaminarayan Chowk, near Sardar Bridge in Adajan was established in 1985, with the murti pratishtha (idol installation) ceremony performed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj in 1996. Affiliated with the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS), it is built in pink sandstone in the traditional Gujarati style with intricate carvings, set in manicured gardens. The mandir serves as a centre of devotion, education, and community service, running charitable initiatives such as health camps and educational programs.

name: Shri Swaminarayan Temple, Surat
town_description: Surat is a major city in Gujarat on the banks of the Tapi River, historically one of India's most important ports under Mughal and then British rule. Today it is a thriving metropolis known worldwide as a diamond-processing and textile-manufacturing hub. The city grew from a 12th-century settlement into a Mughal port and later a British stronghold, retaining colonial-era landmarks, old-city bazaars, and a fast-developing riverfront. It is well connected by air, rail, and road to Mumbai, Vadodara, and the rest of Gujarat.

travel.road: Pramukh Swami Maharaj Marg, Swaminarayan Chowk, Adajan, near Sardar Bridge; reachable by city bus, auto-rickshaw, and taxi
